items.title: HexCon26 product and feature announcements: What’s new and why it matters
items.text:
The HexCon26 opening keynote laid out Hexnode’s broader direction: bringing endpoint management, security, identity and employee experience closer together while using AI and automation to reduce the routine work that falls on IT teams.
Across HexCon26, Hexnode also introduced a new product and a wide range of capabilities spanning orchestration, endpoint management, patching, remote support, identity, migration and day-to-day administration.
At the center of those announcements was Hexnode Synapse.
Hexnode Synapse brings agentic orchestration across IT and security
Hexnode Synapse is an agentic orchestration layer designed to act across endpoint, identity and threat state.
The problem it addresses is familiar. An incident might begin with a ticket, generate an XDR alert and trigger an identity signal, but each event may still live in a different system. In that model, people become the integration layer, moving between consoles and coordinating every handoff manually.
Synapse is designed to connect those signals and coordinate what happens next.
Synapse is currently being opened through an invite-only beta, with initial experiences centered on agent-driven triage, onboarding and incident workflows.
Hexnode UEM Mobile Admin App takes administration beyond the desk
Not every incident waits until an administrator is sitting in front of the UEM console.

items.title: HexCon26 Opening Keynote: Key Announcements and Takeaways
items.text:
HexCon26 kicked off in Atlanta on September 9, with the opening keynote bringing together the event’s biggest themes and announcements.
Apu Pavithran, Founder and CEO of Hexnode, took the stage first, followed by Rachana Vijayan, EVP of Global Go-To-Market and CMO. Together, they laid out where enterprise IT is heading, what Hexnode has built over the past year, and why the company believes the industry is moving from managed devices to managed outcomes.
Here’s a recap of everything announced.
Hexnode is moving from device management to managed outcomes
One of the strongest themes of the keynote was that the job of endpoint management has not fundamentally changed over the years.
IT teams still enroll, configure, patch, secure and troubleshoot devices. What has changed is everything happening through those devices: applications, identity, data, security and increasingly AI.
Hexnode’s direction is therefore centered on autonomy: routine work should increasingly happen on its own, while IT retains control over the policies, approvals and outcomes that matter.
The goal is simple: less time spent on enrolling, patching, chasing and ticketing, and more time spent on the work that actually moves the business forward.
Hexnode AI is becoming the intelligence layer across the platform

items.title: How Does Hexnode XDR Protect Windows and macOS Endpoints?
items.text:
Why Securing Mixed Windows and macOS Fleets Is Getting Harder
Hexnode XDR Windows macOS protection becomes harder when security teams manage each operating system through separate tools. Organizations may use different security agents, policies, consoles, and investigation workflows for Windows and macOS, depending on their security stack. As a result, administrators cannot always apply consistent security controls across the entire fleet.
This fragmentation creates several operational problems:
Separate consoles force analysts to switch tools during investigations and compare data manually.
Inconsistent policy enforcement creates different security baselines for Windows and macOS endpoints.
Fragmented visibility prevents teams from viewing endpoint activity through one consistent operational lens.
Uneven response capabilities can limit how quickly analysts contain threats on each operating system.
Attackers can exploit these gaps by targeting endpoints with weaker monitoring or slower response coverage. Moreover, they can use compromised accounts, shared applications, cloud services, or network access to move across hybrid environments. The MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise matrix reflects this reality by mapping techniques across Windows, macOS, and other platforms.
